articleTitle: Improving Lithium-ion Battery Life Prediction with an Enhanced Multi-Layer Perceptron Model Featuring Autoencoder-Based Feature Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: This study proposes an improved multi-layer perceptron (MLP) model based on autoencoder(AE) feature extraction to predict the life of lithium-ion batteries. In this study, the dimensions of the battery status data were firstly reduced by the autoencoder, and then the extracted features were used to train the MLP model to improve the prediction accuracy of the remaining useful life (RUL) of the battery. In addition, this study also discussed the changes of battery performance at different charging rates, and verified the superiority of the proposed AE-MLP model in predicting the life of lithium batteries at different charging rates by comparing with the prior art. The results show that the AE-MLP model is superior to the traditional MLP model in terms of prediction accuracy and robustness.

articleTitle: Research on the Characteristics of Local Discharge Ground Wave Sensors in New Energy Stations
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: There are many 35 kV cable lines in new energy stations, and the frequency of faults is also high. Cable faults are an important factor affecting the safe and stable operation of new energy. Partial discharge, as an early indicator of insulation degradation in power equipment, has been proven to be an effective fault warning information. Conducting partial discharge detection in distribution network lines can timely detect potential insulation defects or faults and provide new solutions to improve the level of distribution network operation and maintenance. Therefore, it is necessary to conduct research on the performance of partial discharge sensor materials, turns, and other characteristics of power equipment in new energy stations, and design a partial discharge detection device suitable for the characteristics of new energy stations. This device can effectively provide early warnings for partial discharge in new energy stations and is of great significance for the safe and stable operation of new energy stations. TEV sensor is a sensor used to detect the transient ground voltage generated during partial discharge of high-voltage equipment. When partial discharge occurs, pulsating voltage is induced on the surface of the ferromagnetic shell of high-voltage equipment. TEV sensors, as transient ground voltage couplers, can detect the waveform and amplitude of this pulsating voltage, providing a basis for judging and locating partial discharge in high-voltage equipment. Therefore, optimizing the performance design of TEV sensors can effectively improve the detection level of partial discharge.

articleTitle: A study of determining sampling interval and duration for demand factor
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Based on the working condition analysis of plant loads, the comparison of the measured load data of several chemical plants and the derivation of sampling interval and frequency from the perspective of probability, the formula is obtained. Combined with the actual operation of a chemical plant in China, the method of determining sampling interval and time is proposed, Compared with the existing measurement schemes, the sampling duration can be reduced by more than half.

articleTitle: Research on the downscaling method of meteorological data in the spatial boundary layer of power grid
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Typhoons are intense meteorological disasters that significantly damage coastal areas and islands. Accurately predicting typhoon wind field distribution is crucial for disaster prevention and emergency management. This paper investigates a downscaling prediction method for typhoon wind fields based on meteorological monitoring data and applied to real cases. The validity and accuracy of the method are verified by comparing the observation data and prediction results. The results show that the method can provide reliable prediction of typhoon wind fields, which provides an important scientific basis for typhoon disaster prevention and mitigation.

articleTitle: Research on China’s Provincial Power Accounting Method from the Perspective of Carbon Quota
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Based on the rational allocation of carbon quotas, considering the attribution of indirect emissions of electricity, three different calculation methods are used to account for the electricity emissions of various provinces in China from 2008 to 2017. On the one hand, through the comparative analysis of the three methods, the electricity carbon under different principles is studied The changes in emissions, on the other hand, provide a basis for the allocation of carbon quotas for power companies, which is conducive to enhancing the potential and level of enterprises’ emission reduction production.

articleTitle: Leveraging Hybrid LSTM-Attention-CatBoost Model for Complex Energy Behavior Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: We present an advanced energy prediction model that addresses energy imbalance by integrating Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) with Attention Mechanism for time-series analysis and categorical boosting (CatBoost) for categorical feature optimization. This model accurately predicts the complex energy behaviors of prosumers who both generate and consume energy. Simulation results show that our model outperforms traditional methods with the lowest Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 48.514. By achieving such a high level of accuracy, this model improves grid operation efficiency, offers a practical solution for smart grid management.

articleTitle: Research on Transmission and Transformation Cost Stability for Carbon Reduction and Market Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: In the context of global economic integration and energy structure transformation, cost control of power transmission and transformation projects has become an important factor affecting the economy and reliability of the power system. This article proposes a cost stabilization technology for power transmission and transformation projects that adapts to the unified market and carbon reduction development, in response to the problems of poor information transmission and inefficient cost management throughout the entire process in current cost management. This article constructs a key indicator system for dynamic cost control throughout the entire process, including five primary indicators: organizational team, construction period, quality, cost, and social environment. Based on the grey relational evaluation method, a corresponding dynamic evaluation model is established. Through empirical analysis of different stages, the effectiveness of the proposed model in improving the scientific and rational cost management of power transmission and transformation projects has been verified.

articleTitle: A mobile UAV hangar design for transmission line inspection
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: With the continuous expansion of the application scale of transmission line UAV(Unmanned Aerial Vehicle) inspection, the existing UAV has its own limiting factors such as short endurance time, positioning accuracy to be improved, and great influence on personnel operation, which affect the application effect of UAV in transmission line operation and maintenance. At present, there are some applications of fixed or mobile UAV hangars. However, limited by size and cost, it has not yet achieved large-scale application. In order to make full use of existing power inspection vehicles, this paper presents a design method of mobile UAV hangar for transmission line inspection applications. The integration of UAV hangar and pickup truck is realized through structure design. At the same time, a UAV landing method based on brightness recognition is proposed and integrated with hangar platform. Through the landing test, the UAV can land in about 1 minute, the landing accuracy meets the size requirements of the take-off and landing platform, and the UAV can be recovered through the centering mechanism. This method lays a strong foundation for the practical application of UAV hangar in line inspection.

articleTitle: Optimal configuration of energy storage for high penetration of flexible resource aggregation in new-type source-load distribution networks
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Based on the characteristic of rich flexibility resources in high penetration new-type source-load distribution networks, and consider first aggregating the flexibility resources within the distribution network into virtual energy storage. Considering the capacity and output characteristics of virtual energy storage, the optimal model of energy storage capacity configuration is constructed with the optimal economy of the whole life cycle. A simulation model is built in CloudlEPS to solve the optimal capacity of energy storage. Compare it with the scenario that does not consider the aggregation of flexibility resources, and verify the advantages of this model in reducing initial investment in energy storage and improving the economic operation of the system.

articleTitle: Carbon Emission Management of Industrial Parks Based on Carbon Price and Electricity Consumption Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Driven by carbon neutrality ambitions, effective carbon emission management has become paramount for industrial park sustainability. This study proposes an industrial park carbon emission management model incorporating carbon price and electricity consumption predictions. By leveraging historical data and machine learning algorithms, separate prediction models for carbon price and electricity consumption are developed. These predictions, combined with park-specific carbon emission intensity data, enable forecasting future carbon emissions. The model further incorporates government carbon policies and park emission reduction targets to formulate data-driven management strategies. Results demonstrate the model’s effectiveness in predicting carbon emission trends and providing scientific emission reduction recommendations, facilitating the achievement of carbon neutrality goals within industrial parks.

articleTitle: Short-term Electricity Load Prediction and Carbon Emissions Based on Synchrosqueezing Wavelet Transform and Nested Long Short-Term Memory
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Accurately predicting that short-term electricity load and carbon emissions are essential for optimizing energy structure, reducing carbon emissions and achieving sustainable development. This article proposes a short-term electricity load carbon emission prediction method based on Synchrosqueezing Wavelet Transform (SWT) and Nested Long Short-Term Memory (NLSTM) neural network. First of all, by introducing SWT to improve the model forecasting accuracy, the electricity load data is decomposed. Then enter the decomposed data input to NLSTM neural network for training and prediction, solving the difficulty of extraction of ordinary Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural networks for the periodic features of the original electricity load, and a problem of randomness in model parameter selection. Finally, combined with the local electricity carbon emissions factor, the predicted value of carbon emissions is finally obtained. The experimental results show that this method has higher predictive accuracy compared to variational mode decomposition (VMD) and single neural network model, providing an effective means for electricity load prediction and refined management of carbon emissions.

Author Keywords: Short-term electricity load prediction and carbon emissions
Nested Long Short Term Memory neural networks

articleTitle: Research on intelligent identification method of lightning arrester deterioration state based on GASFCNN
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: In recent years, monitoring and identifying the deterioration state of surge arresters has become essential for enhancing the reliability of electrical power systems. This paper introduces a novel method for recognizing the deterioration state of surge arresters, employing Gramian Angular Summation Fields (GASF) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN). Initially, GASF technology is utilized to transform the historical operational data of surge arresters into image format, capturing the texture and structural features that characterize the deterioration state. Subsequently, a specially designed CNN model processes these images to extract features and perform classification, thus identifying the deterioration states accurately. The results of this research offer a new approach for the online recognition of deterioration states in critical protective devices on transmission lines, providing significant insights for the safe and reliable operation of power systems.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Distribution Automation System and Its Application in Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: To study the design and realization of DMI and its application in Intelligent Grid, this paper puts forward a study on how to design and implement DMI in Intelligent Grid. The conception of automatic distribution system is analysed in this paper. Through the application of DNE in the electric power system, the transformation of electric power administration can be facilitated to be refined, intensified, and more efficient, so as to enhance the economic performance of the electricity suppliers, and to offer high quality electricity supply to the local economy. In the end, the author gives a case study on the implementation of DNE project and sums up its applied effect in order to enhance its running and maintaining management.

articleTitle: Improved YOLOv8 for substation image tampering detection
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: In modern power systems, the integrity and authenticity of image data are critical. However, image tampering can lead to misjudgments and erroneous decisions, threatening the safe and stable operation of substation. To address this issue, we propose an improved YOLOv8 model specifically designed for efficiently detecting tampered areas in power images. By introducing the Extra Deepwise Convolution(ExtraDW) module, optimizing the Spatial Pyramid Pooling module, and proposing the Cross Stage Featrue Pyramid(CSFP) module, we have enhanced the model’s accuracy in detecting tampered regions in complex backgrounds and improved the detection speed to meet the real-time requirements of power scenarios. Experimental results show that the proposed model performs excellently in all performance metrics, achieving an ideal balance of high precision and accuracy. The model’s speed is 96.49 FPS higher than the best existing model with similar detection accuracy, demonstrating its outstanding performance in substation scenarios and its capability to meet the demands of efficient real-time detection.

articleTitle: A Prediction-Correction Based Method for Calculating the Affine Carbon Flow in Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Carbon flow calculation methods, which can allocate the direct carbon emissions generated during unit power generation to the load side in the form of indirect carbon emissions, have become an important means of driving consumers to reduce carbon emissions. However, due to the fluctuation of loads and renewable energy sources, the system carbon emission intensity cannot be fully predicted in advance. Therefore, this paper proposes an affine carbon emission flow calculation method for measuring the trend and interval of the system carbon emission flow under a certain level of uncertainty effect. First, for the discontinuity of the carbon emission flow model, the carbon modes are divided according to the branch power flow direction of the whole network, and all possible carbon modes are identified based on Kirchhoff’s law and the analytical nature of the affine noise elements. Second, for the nonlinearity of carbon emission flow, new noise elements are constructed in the calculation of each carbon mode based on the idea of prediction-correction to ensure the completeness of the calculation. IEEE14 simulations show that the method proposed in this paper takes less than 7% of the time of the Monte Carlo method and has an average conservatism of less than 6%.

articleTitle: A Multi-Stage Vehicle-to-Vehicle Wireless Power Transfer System
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) are becoming more and more popular in society because they do not produce harmful gases and have the advantage of being energy efficient and environmentally friendly. EVs need to be charged at charging stations, but charging stations can be overcrowded during peak charging times due to inadequate infrastructure. In this paper, a multi-stage vehicle-to-vehicle (V 2 V) wireless charging system is proposed, which can facilitate one-to-many charging, thereby alleviating congestion at charging stations. To meet different usage requirements, different strategies are switched to change different modes. To save the space and manufacturing cost of the EVs, the switches of the system are multiplexed. Theoretical and experimental models are built. The experimental results are consistent with the theoretical values, which verifies the feasibility of the proposed system.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Algorithms for Fault Detection and Localization in Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive comparative analysis of four machine learning algorithms (SVM, DT, FNN, RF) for fault detection and localization in photovoltaic (PV) systems. The study aims to address the limitations of traditional methods, such as manual inspections and rule-based approaches, which can be time-consuming, error-prone, and inflexible. By leveraging advanced machine learning techniques, we aim to improve the accuracy, efficiency, and scalability of fault detection and localization in PV systems. We conducted a rigorous evaluation of these algorithms using a unified dataset and performance metrics, focusing on common faults like shading, open circuit, and short circuit. Our findings demonstrate the superior performance of Random Forest (RF) for both fault classification and localization tasks, highlighting its potential for enhancing the reliability and efficiency of PV systems.

articleTitle: Analysis of GIS Insulation Fault Characteristics under VFTO
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Basin insulators are one of the rare faults with high probability in GIS equipment, especially the surface flashover of basin insulators, which poses a great threat to the safety of GIS operation. This article analyzes the II bus fault that occurred in the 220 kV GIS substation. Through the fault waveform and equipment damage, it was found that the fault was caused by the operating overvoltage generated when the circuit breaker was closed. To further analyze the fault, this article established an electric field simulation model to conduct electric field simulation analysis on the GIS bus under operating overvoltage and short-circuit grounding faults. The results indicate that the asymmetry of the bowl-shaped insulator structure exacerbates the occurrence of faults, and overvoltage and short-circuit grounding during operation lead to insulator breakdown.

articleTitle: Research on microgrid control technology based on patent analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Search on patent applications for microgrid control technology was conducted on a global scale, analyzing the development lifecycle, main applicants, technology development direction, important patents, and overseas patent layout of microgrid control technology. From the results, it can be seen that microgrid control technology has gone through two stages, namely the technology start-up period and technology development period. Patent technologies are mainly concentrated in categories such as H02J3, G02J13, and G06Q50. Overall, the research focus of microgrid control technology is to improve the stability, reliability, coordination, and economy of control systems. Research on improving power quality and operation flexibility can be further studied. Based on the analysis of the main applicants’ patent technology, important patents, and overseas patent layout, it is recommended that relevant Chinese enterprises increase their research on smart control technology and pay attention to the layout of patents.

articleTitle: Simulation Study of the Effect of Coil Parameters on Electromagnetic Forces
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: When ice cover occurs on transmission lines, the attachment of ice increases the weight of the transmission line, resulting in greater mechanical loads on the line. Ice can also lead to phase-to-phase short circuits or ground faults, affecting the reliability of the power supply. The electric pulse de-icing device can be used for transmission lines and other linear structures, and the de-icing effect of the electric pulse de-icing device is mainly affected by the coil. In this paper, different sizes of coils are studied, and the changes of magnetic field, eddy current and pulse force under different coil parameters are analyzed to study the electric-magnetic-force coupling process when the electric pulse acts. The results show that when the number of coil turns is the same, the coil wound with $4 \times 0.4 \mathrm{~mm}$ enameled wire produces a better pulse effect than the coil wound with $2 \times 0.4 \mathrm{~mm}$ enameled wire; with the increase of the number of coil turns, the effect of the pulse effect is getting better and better. This paper can provide ideas for the development of electric pulse de-icing device.

articleTitle: Reversible retrofit to hydro plants for better renewables consumption in Central China
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Substituting coal electricity with renewables is the fundamental measure to achieve carbon neutrality in China. However, the intermittency and the poor flexibility of power systems hinders the accommodation of renewables. Here, we put forward a new concept of reversible hydro plants that enable charging and discharging operation modes which are similar to pumped hydro but have lower construction costs. An integrated planning model is proposed to identify the benefits. First, a cost estimation model was constructed to identify the development potential and retrofit costs. Then, a planning model embedded with hourly dispatch for power systems is built to optimize the retrofit decision on reversible hydro plants. Finally, the power systems of Central China were applied to validate the benefits and generate the optimized retrofit plan. Results show that the reversible hydropower retrofit can effectively decrease the renewable curtailment and operation costs in Central China.

articleTitle: Machine learning modeling and predictive control of nonlinear boiler-turbine unit
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: The boiler-turbine unit (BTU) is extensively utilizeed in power generation owing to its high reliability and operation flexibility. However, the control design of BTU system remains challenging due to its intricate dynamic properties, such as wide range of nonlinearities, large inertia, and strong coupling in multivariable systems. More challengingly, it is generally difficult and time-consuming to derive an accurate nonlinear model to capture the BTU dynamics and facilitate controller design. In this regard, machine learning methods show great potential in classical engineering fields, such as modeling nonlinear dynamic systems. In this article, a machine learning based model predictive control (MPC) scheme is presented for the nonlinear BTU. The machine learning method is first adopted to model the BTU using the input and output data directly, which can also be used to model a large class of nonlinear dynamic systems. Then, this data-driven model is deployed as a predictive model in the MPC for optimal control of the nonlinear BTU. Finally, a series of simulations are performed to validate the proposed method, including RNN training and testing, open-loop prediction simulation and closed-loop control simulation.

articleTitle: Dynamic evolutions of local current density and water distribution in dead-end proton exchange membrane fuel cell
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: The anode and cathode dead-end proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) has complex water management problems. The performance will change drastically in the deadend mode. Stable performance output is the key to the application of lunar PEMFC. This study established a single-channel three-dimensional two-phase transient model under the dead-end mode, and verified the model by combining experiments under steady-state and dynamic state. The effects of different loads and anodecathode inlet humidity on the output performance and the distribution of water and current density of the dead-end PEMFC were analyzed. The simulation results show that the performance change of PEMFC is closely related to the accumulation of liquid water, and the initial performance is closely related to the membrane water content. Local accumulation of liquid water can lead to a severe decline in performance.

articleTitle: Research on the Method of Balancing Electricity Quantity in Rural New Power Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: With the proposal of the national goal of “carbon neutrality and peak carbon emissions”, the proportion of new energy connected to the power grid is increasing, and the power balance characteristics of the power system have undergone significant changes. Compared with urban distribution networks, rural power grids have the characteristics of distributed wind and solar energy storage, long power supply radius, long distance, high line losses, and low reliability. The paper constructs a new rural power grid power balance model that includes wind, solar, storage, and load, and proposes a power balance calculation method based on particle swarm optimization algorithm. The experimental results show that the model and method proposed in the paper have achieved good power and energy balance effects. It can effectively reduce the abandoned electricity and system disturbance of new energy.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control for Voltage Control in Wind Farms
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: This paper proposes a model-based predictive control to regulate the voltage for a wind farm. The active session of the wind farm controller (WFC) is a proportional controller that allocates the dispatch power to each turbine in proportion to the available power of each turbine. The reactive session regulates the optimal output of the wind turbines (WTGs) and SVG, stabilizes the POC and WTG node voltages as well as retains the maximum fast reactive capacity by means of MPC. In order to improve the computational efficiency and effectively solve the convergence-related problems, this paper adopts the analytical method of sensitivity coefficients for calculation. In order to verify the feasibility of the method, a wind farm model consisting of 20 wind turbines and one SVG is designed to assess the feasibility of the method. The experimental results show that the wind farm model can effectively improve the control accuracy and performance of the wind farm.

articleTitle: Transformer fault diagnosis based on Bayes active learning
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Dissolved Gas Analysis (DGA) is the most commonly used method for on-site power transformer fault diagnosis. Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques enhance fault diagnosis but rely on large amounts of labeled data. Active learning optimizes this by selectively querying uncertain, informative samples for manual labeling, which reduces costs and improves diagnostic accuracy with minimal number of labeled data. This paper introduces an innovative Bayes Active Learning Method based Entropy Sampling Strategy(BALM-ESS) that employs entropy-based sampling strategy in active learning process to select the most valuable samples for training. The method is validated using the IEC TC10 dataset and is compared with Bayes Random sampling (BRS) which randomly selecting some samples from the unlabeled sample. The findings demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm and its robustness in tackling classification problems by spending as few labeled samples as possible.

articleTitle: Prediction of Insulators Ice Types Driven by Icing Images and Micrometeorology Time Series Fusion Data
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Ice accumulation on overhead transmission lines poses significant risks to the stability of power grids. Precise ice types prediction can help power grid assess future freezing risk and prevent icing incidents. This study introduces a data-driven method for insulator ice types prediction, utilizing a fusion of images and micrometeorological data of the previous three days. Based on the icing monitoring data from China Southern Power Grid from 2014 to 2021, the approach fused images with micrometeorological time series for the first 3 days at 6 intervals to create a data fusion dataset. The insulator ice type prediction model, based on eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) technology, was trained and tested using 4,503 and 1,931 samples, respectively. Its precision and recall reached 97.2%, which verified the accuracy of the proposed method and predicted the future insulator ice types.

articleTitle: A Flexible Holomorphic Embedding Method for Integrated Gas and Electricity System
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Energy flow calculation is the basis of system planning and optimal scheduling. However, the traditional energy flow calculation method has the problems of sensitive initial value selection and slow convergence in complex scenarios. In this paper, an energy flow calculation method based on flexible holomorphic embedding in the Integrated Gas and Electricity System is proposed. Based on the construction of a flexible holomorphic embedding model, the power series coefficients of the state variables of the system are recursively solved, and the energy flow distribution of the system is obtained. Simulation experiments verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm, and show advantages in computational efficiency and convergence performance compared with Newton Raphson method.

articleTitle: Design on Intelligent Monitoring and Management Platform for Overhead Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: With the increasingly complex external operating environment of transmission lines, the whole society’s demand for power supply reliability continues to improve. To ensure the stable operation of overhead transmission lines, this paper proposes an intelligent monitoring and management platform for overhead transmission lines based on advanced technology. Based on digital twin technology, the platform constructs real and highly simulated transmission line scenes, and at the same time combines transmission line ontology modelling, tree growth prediction, real-time access and display of channel monitoring data, conductor arc droop simulation and wind deviation calculation, capacity increase analysis of carrying capacity, tower force simulation, early warning analysis and other functions, which comprehensively improves the monitoring and management level of transmission lines. Through this platform, operators can monitor the status of transmission lines in real time, quickly find potential problems and take corresponding measures. The application of prediction algorithms makes the prediction of the growth of surrounding vegetation more accurate, effectively preventing the impact of vegetation on transmission lines. Functions such as conductor arc sag simulation, wind deviation calculation and tower force simulation provide scientific basis for the safety and stability of transmission lines.

articleTitle: Research on distributed temperature monitoring technology of transformer based on variational mode decomposition
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Transformer temperature monitoring is important to power system operation and maintenance. However, there is currently a lack of in-situ monitoring methods for the internal temperature of power transformers. This paper proposes a new type of transformer temperature in-situ monitoring scheme. With the help of the characteristics of the sensing optical fiber, which is not subject to electromagnetic interference, small adhesion, and non-metallic materials, the distributed Raman temperature measurement technology is used to realize the in-situ accurate measurement of the temperature of the three-phase winding and the oil tank area of the transformer. A 10 kV oil-immersed transformer prototype was successfully developed, and the internal temperature variation law of the transformer was obtained by a short-circuit temperature rise test. At the same time, a Raman temperature denoising algorithm based on variational mode decomposition and Pearson correlation coefficient is proposed, which realizes the accurate measurement of the internal temperature of the transformer and provides a new scheme for online monitoring of transformer temperature.

articleTitle: A Dual-Field Coupled Dynamic Model for Optimizing Compressed Air Energy Storage System Performance and Fault Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: As global energy demand rises and renewable energy integration increases, electrical grids face growing challenges in balancing supply and demand. Compressed Air Energy Storage (CAES) technology has emerged as a promising solution to enhance grid stability by storing excess energy during low-demand periods and releasing it during peak loads. This research focuses on optimizing the dynamic performance of CAES systems by constructing a dual-field coupled dynamic model that integrates both aerodynamic and thermal processes. The study applies a modular modeling approach to simulate key components, including the compressor, air storage tanks, turbine, and heat storage tanks. By leveraging advanced methodologies from recent studies on adiabatic CAES systems, the model aims to improve system efficiency and dynamic response. Fault mechanisms, characteristic parameters, and operational modes are analyzed to ensure safe and reliable system operation. The simulation results reveal crucial insights into the thermodynamic behavior of the system, providing a foundation for optimization and fault diagnosis.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Value Assessment Method for Energy Big Data Based on Data Value Chain
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Through the deep integration and intelligent analysis of energy big data, comprehensive perception, accurate prediction and optimization control of the energy system can be realized, but the problem of data value assessment has become one of the obstacles restricting the development of energy big data. This paper proposes a comprehensive value assessment method for energy big data based on the data value chain. It aims to construct a multi-dimensional assessment index system by comprehensively considering the value creation process of energy big data in data collection, processing, analysis and application. The core idea is to use the data value chain as a framework to decompose the value assessment of energy big data into multiple stages, and to design corresponding indicators for each stage, covering economic value, social value and environmental value, in order to comprehensively assess the integrated value of energy big data. The core idea is to use the data value chain as a framework to decompose the value assessment of energy big data into multiple stages and design corresponding indicators for each stage. It covers the aspects of economic value, social value and environmental value in order to comprehensively assess the comprehensive value of energy big data. And a case study is taken to prove the effectiveness of the proposed model, which provides a scientific basis for the effective use and value realization of energy big data.

articleTitle: An Inductive and Capacitive Hybrid Wireless Power Transfer System for Consumer Electronics with Shared Components
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Wireless power transfer (WPT) technology is more convenient and flexible than traditional wired charging technology, which can eliminate the metal wire connection between the power supply and the load. In this paper, a wireless charging system which combines inductive power transfer (IPT) and capacitive power transfer (CPT) circuits for desktop is proposed. The system can realize the two working modes of IPT and CPT respectively, and users can switch the charging mode according to the specific use scenario and charging demand. Both IPT and CPT circuits adopt the series-series compensation, which has the advantages of a simple structure and high efficiency. In this paper, the theoretical analysis and derivation of the circuit topology under the two operating modes are carried out, and the parameter design process is given. Finally, the validity of the system is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Dynamic Carbon Quota Gap Prediction and Rolling Optimization Based on Temporal Fusion Transformer and Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: As global efforts to mitigate climate change intensify, efficient carbon quota management has become critical for enterprises to meet emission reduction targets. Traditional carbon quota allocation models often struggle to adapt to dynamic market conditions and diverse enterprise needs, especially for those transitioning to clean energy. This study addresses the challenge by proposing a novel approach that integrates the Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) model with reinforcement learning to predict carbon quota gaps and optimize quota management strategies. The method leverages time series forecasting to accurately predict future carbon emissions and employs reinforcement learning to dynamically adjust production strategies based on carbon quota gaps. The main contribution of this research lies in its ability to not only forecast emissions but also adaptively optimize quota management in response to real-time conditions. Experimental results demonstrate the method’s effectiveness in reducing carbon emissions and managing quota gaps, particularly in industries facing variable market demands and regulatory environments. This approach offers a flexible, data-driven solution for enterprises, including those with advanced electrification, aiming to enhance carbon quota efficiency and transition towards carbon neutrality.

articleTitle: Prediction and optimization scheduling of wind and solar new energy generation based on big data
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: In order to ensure the efficient operation of the power transmission system, reduce the daily maintenance costs of the power grid, and thus improve the security and stability of the power grid, it is necessary to correctly and optimally calculate the power of wind energy and photovoltaics. power generation.. This paper provides a brief introduction to the characteristics of electricity generation and photovoltaics, and a brief description and analysis of new wind and solar forecasting models based on RBF neural networks to achieve accurate and efficient forecasting of wind and solar power. and reduce the problems that arise during the production and use of energy.

articleTitle: Research on the Influencing Factors of Energy Big Data Value Based on DEMATEL-ISM Model
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Clarifying the influencing factors of energy big data value is an important part of releasing the value of energy big data assets and promoting the in-depth development of the energy industry, but the current research on the influence factors of energy big data value is relatively lacking. Therefore, based on the energy big data value chain, this paper analyzes the influencing factors affecting the whole link from energy big data value generation to value realization. Then, it establishes the DEMATEL-ISM model. Finally, it optimizes and screens the factor set based on the DEMATEL-ISM model, clarifies the intrinsic structural relationship among the factors, and reveals the key influencing factors and the degree of influence.

articleTitle: Sensorless Control System of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Optimized by Super-Twisting Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: The traditional sliding mode observer (SMO) has low observation accuracy and high-frequency buffeting in the non-inductive control system of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM), with slow response speed and weak anti-disturbance ability. The control strategy of superspiral sliding mode observer (STSMO), which combines the superspiral algorithm (STA) and sliding mode observer (SMO), is proposed for the problem of excessive overshoot. This method uses continuous function G(s) instead of discontinuous sgn(s) to improve the accuracy of the rotor position measurement, reduce buffering, and enhance its robustness. The simulation results show that the system can accurately measure the rotational speed and rotor position, and the rotational speed error value around -3r/min. Compared with the traditional SMO control, the rotational speed recovery time is reduced by 67%, and there is almost no overshoot, which has stronger robustness and strong practical application value in motor control.

articleTitle: Parameter optimization method of energy storage controller based on power system transient stability
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Battery energy storage system plays an important role in calming wind and wind power volatility and maintaining system safety and stability. In view of the parameter optimization of the controller of the energy storage system, considering the impact of the energy storage system on the transient stability of the power system, data interaction was realized by studying the interface configuration between DIgSILENT and Python, and optimization code of co-simulation was written based on Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm. A parameter optimization method of energy storage controller based on DIgSILENT-Python is proposed. Finally, the IEEE9-node system is used to analyze the optimization method. The experimental results verify that the co-simulation framework can effectively optimize the parameters of the energy storage controller, which solves the problem that DIgSILENT can only set the components with measurement functions as the optimization target, and is suitable for a number of circuit faults in the system. It can guarantee the safe and stable operation of power system.

articleTitle: A Fault Arc Circuit Breaker Based on Arc Voltage and Short-circuit Current Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: This paper developed an arc fault circuit breaker capable of effectively identifying both series and parallel are faults, as well as limiting the output quantity of arc faults, which is particularly useful in renewable energy systems such as photovoltaic and wind power setups to mitigate the risks associated with DC arc faults. Series arc faults are identified by detecting arc voltage using a voltage sensor, while parallel arc faults are detected through short-circuit current limitation using a current sensor. By adding a current-limiting switch, the output quantity of arc faults is effectively controlled. Experiments on both series and parallel arc faults were conducted, and the results showed that the proposed arc fault circuit breaker can effectively identify series and parallel arc faults and control the output quantity of arc faults. Additionally, a miss detection and false operation test was designed, with a miss detection rate of $\mathbf{2. 5 \%}$ and a false operation rate of only $\mathbf{3. 3 3 \%}$, effectively verifying the safety of the proposed arc fault circuit breaker. This device has significant implications for the development and testing of are fault detectors.

articleTitle: Short-Term Load Forecasting Method Based on Improved Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Traditional power load forecasting methods often struggle to handle the long-term nonlinear trends in sequence data, which can result in inadequate forecasting accuracy in practical applications, affecting the normal operation of power systems. Therefore, this paper proposes an improved Transformer model to capture the long-term nonlinear trends in power load time series. The model utilizes a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) in the encoder to capture short-term dependencies within the forecast horizon and integrates a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network with a self-attention mechanism in the decoder to capture long-range dependencies by incorporating periodic components of the power load. This addresses the issue of losing periodic data features due to excessively long load sequences. Additionally, Lagrange interpolation and normalization techniques are used to handle outliers and uneven data distribution in the power load data, ensuring the validity of input data and improving forecasting accuracy at the data level. Experimental results show that, compared to commonly used models like Convolutional Neural Networks-Gate Recurrent Unit (CNN-GRU-Attention) the forecasting error decreases by $\mathbf{3. 4 \% - 5. 3 \%}$.

articleTitle: Non-singular Fast Terminal Sliding Mode Control of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Linear Motor Based on Superhelix Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: A novel non-singular fast terminal sliding mode control (NFTSMC) based on super torsional sliding mode Observer (STA-STO) was designed to solve the problems such as obvious buffeting, slow convergence time to reach surface of mucus and unknown disturbance in sliding mode control of permanent magnet synchronous linear motor (PMLSM). Frist, the non-singular fast terminal sliding mode surface is used to shorten the convergence time and eliminate the singularity problem. Then, a super helical synovial observer for sensor less position detection is introduced. Finally, the symbol function of the observer is expressed as a continuous function and get a new observer. Better than the traditional synovial observer, This observer significantly suppresses shaking.

Author Keywords: nonsingular fast terminal sliding mode control

articleTitle: Frequency Control Method of Isolated Micro-grid With Virtual Synchronous Generator Mode Switching
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: In view of the problem that the adjustment effect of the traditional PI-based frequency control method is not efficient in the asymmetric operation state of the micro-grid, a frequency control method based on the mode switching of the virtual synchronous generator (VSG) is designed. Specifically, firstly, on the frequency regulation of PI controller in the asymmetric operating state, the influence mechanism of the double fundamental frequency component is analyzed. Secondly, the mode switching method is designed to judge the operating state of the power grid by the asymmetric degree matrix. Thirdly, aiming at the asymmetric operation state, the effective control of microgrid frequency is realized by introducing integral to eliminate the double fundamental frequency component to obtain new data of active power. Finally, under asymmetric operating conditions, comparative experiments, which verifies the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method, show that the proposed method has more advantages in reducing frequency deviation and frequency fluctuation.

articleTitle: Research on representative day selection method based on grey relational and K-means clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: With the rapid development of renewable energy technology, Distributed Generation (DG) has become an important component of the power system. The integration of distributed power sources not only improves the flexibility and reliability of power systems, but also brings new challenges to load forecasting, grid scheduling, and line loss calculation in power systems. In response to the problem of selecting representative days for theoretical line loss calculation, this paper considers the impact of distributed power generation on the power system and proposes a representative day selection method based on grey correlation and k-means clustering. Firstly, the grey correlation method is used to select the top ten indicators that are related to the daily line loss rate. Then, the K-means clustering analysis method is used to cluster the top ten indicators, divide the substation data into three categories, select the most effective clustering center, and calculate the distance between the substation data and the clustering center on a monthly basis. The closest day to the clustering center is used as the representative day of this month. Finally, experimental data from Zhuhai was selected to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Research on Microgrid Capacity Planning based on Cooperative Game
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: To address the problem of cost sharing among multiple economic agents participating in microgrid capacity planning, it is proposed that the formulation of binding agreements is the key to the cooperative game that can be realized ultimately. Firstly, the conditions that need to be satisfied by the cost sharing strategy of cooperative game in islanded wind-photo-hydrogen storage microgrid system are given, i.e., overall rationality, coalition rationality and individual rationality. Secondly, four cost-sharing strategies are used to cost-share the total economic cost in the fully cooperative game, and the acceptance degree of each game participant in the cooperative game process is measured by the MDP (modified disruption propensity, MDP) index. Finally, taking the actual wind speed and light intensity of a place in Northwest China as an example, it is verified that the cost sharing strategy based on equal MDP index and Shapley value is more attractive to all parties and belongs to the core set, which is a binding cost sharing strategy.

articleTitle: Energy Planning of Green Park: Based on the Case of Nantong Economic Zone
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: This paper outlines a comprehensive energy service model for green parks in Nantong, a city in Jiangsu Province, which possesses robust economic growth potential and abundant renewable energy resources. The proposed model aims to integrate advanced energy technologies, enhance energy reliability, and improve energy efficiency while contributing to the national goals of carbon reduction. By exploring the energy needs and infrastructure of Nantong’s green industrial parks, the paper lays the foundation for a scalable, sustainable energy service solution.

articleTitle: K-means Clustering Study on the Evolution Rule of Ice Thickness for Segmental Prediction of Icing Process
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Ice cover prediction is of great significance for judging the future ice cover situation and arranging ice melting work in advance. In this paper, 11 ice cover characteristic parameters describing the ice thickness-time curve of ice cover events are proposed, as well as the methods of normalization and hierarchical K-Means clustering. The 282 ice-covering events were clustered three times, and four types of ice-cover thickness change patterns were obtained, namely, spike type, saturated type, multi-peak type and artificial ice melting type, and their regular characteristics were summarized and analyzed. Based on the clustering results of the type of ice cover thickness change rule, the distribution law of the relevant parameters such as the voltage level where the line is located, the year of ice cover, the number of days of ice cover and the maximum ice cover thickness were statistically analyzed, which laid the foundation for the fine prediction of ice cover on transmission lines.

articleTitle: Design of electric vehicle wireless charging simulation rescue system based on LCC
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: With the acceleration of industrialization and the needs of social development, traditional automobile fault rescue methods cannot be effectively applied to electric vehicles. This paper adopts a bilateral LCC compensation network, designs a transmitter and a receiver respectively to complete the fault simulation rescue for electric vehicles lacking energy, and simulates the coil model through Ansys Maxwell to analyze the influence of the parameters of the coil model on the power transmission of the system. The test results show that the system’s anti-drift capability and transmission efficiency are improved, and the theoretical and simulation results are consistent.

articleTitle: The P2D model for a lithium-ion cell with particle radius distribution of the active materials
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: The assumption of constant electrode particle radius used in the classic pseudo two-dimensional model cannot meet the requirements for simulation accuracy. This work introduces the electrode particle radius distribution while maintaining the homogenization characteristics of the pseudo two-dimensional model, thereby improving simulation accuracy. The theoretical method of introducing electrode particle radius distribution into the pseudo two-dimensional model was mathematically derived, as well as the correction method for the specific surface area of electrode particles after introducing the electrode particle radius distribution. Finally, simulation verification was carried out on the pseudo-two-dimensional model without and with expanded electrode particle radius distribution based on experimental data. The results indicate that this method can more accurately simulate the polarization changes inside the battery, especially for the simulation of relaxation processes, with higher simulation accuracy.

articleTitle: Study on the effect of optimizing airflow organization on the cooling efficiency of air conditioning in substation secondary equipment rooms
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: The increase in the level of intelligence and automation in substations leads to a large amount of energy consumption. And continuously operating secondary equipment room account for the main energy consumption. Therefore, the adoption of more energy efficient and effective cooling measures is a key development direction for data room. In order to solve the problem of low efficiency and high energy consumption of the air conditioning system of substation data room. This paper takes a 110 kV indoor substation secondary equipment rooms in Beijing as the research object. Through experimental testing and numerical simulation. According to the principle of “cold equipment first, then cold environment”. The airflow organization method of the indoor air conditioning system was optimized and designed. The results show that: under the condition of $80 \%$ of the original air supply volume, the airflow organization form of double-side air supply and double-side air return can not only attenuate the temperature stratification phenomenon and reduce the indoor high temperature area. It can also ensure that the average temperature of the equipment area is lower than $28^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. Improve the effect of indoor ventilation and heat dissipation. At the same time, an appropriate increase in the height of the air supply outlet, the efficiency of the air conditioning system also has a certain degree of improvement. Option 3 can reduce the energy consumption by $\mathbf{5 8. 4 \%}$ compared with the original scheme.

articleTitle: Active Distribution Network Fault Localization based on Improved Chaotic Binary Particle Swarm Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Aiming at the existing intelligent optimization algorithms in Active Distribution Network (ADN) fault localization, such as long-time-consuming fault localization, slow convergence speed, and easy convergence of faults to local optimal solutions, this paper proposes an Improved Chaotic Binary Particle Swarm Algorithm (ICBPSO). Firstly, a switching function reconstruction method is proposed based on the switching function construction characteristics of the ADN section state and node state. Secondly, based on the fault section characteristics of ADN, algorithms such as initial particle swarm sparsification, optimal particle differentiation, and optimal particle mutation are proposed, further improving the Chaotic Binary Particle Swarm Algorithm(CBPSO). Lastly, simulation experiments are used to validate the efficacy of ICBPSO in ADN fault localization. The tests evaluate several ADN fault localization techniques and simulation results show that ICBPSO performs better in fault localization elapsed time and convergence speed.

articleTitle: Safety Monitoring Scheme for Indoor Personnel in Substations based on Helmet Detection and Action Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: This paper presents an indoor positioning and action recognition system based on stereo vision, aiming to achieve a safety monitoring system based on helmet detection and action recognition. The system employs the YOLO v8 model for object detection and pose estimation, enhancing the detection capability for small targets by introducing the P2 layer and BiFPN structure, and realizing model lightweighting with the GhostConv module. The BoT-SORT algorithm is utilized for object tracking to ensure the accuracy of action recognition. Action recognition is performed using the ST-GCN, which extracts human skeleton features through a spatiotemporal graph convolutional network. Additionally, a double-threshold detection framework is designed to effectively segment video clips containing the desired actions. Experimental results indicate that the improved YOLOv8 model has enhanced detection performance. This research provides an effective solution for indoor monitoring scenarios, with high practical value and broad application prospects.

articleTitle: A Novel Fault Current Limiting Method for MMCHVDC System Based on VSG Control in LVRT Process
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: With the wide application of flexible DC transmission technology in the field of power transmission and distribution research, the power electronic characteristics of the power system become more and more obvious, the overall strength is reduced, and the anti-interference ability is weakened. In order to solve this problem, the grid-forming control strategy of converter is proposed. This paper is based on the virtual synchronous generator control technology, so that the grid-connected inverter has the inherent inertia of synchronous generator as well as damping characteristics to improve the overall stability of the system. However, the traditional VSG control will have the problem of fault current overrun when facing the AC grid fault, which may damage the power electronic devices. For this reason, this paper investigates the fault current development mechanism and the fault current limiting method when an ac-side symmetrical fault occurs in a grid-configured MMC under VSG control. The methods of adjusting the reactive power sag coefficient during the fault period and adjusting the virtual internal potential at the fault instant are proposed to realize the fault current limiting control. Finally, simulation verification is carried out based on the MATLAB/Simulink simulation platform, and the results better show the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: A Review of Research on Group Regulation and Control of Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: With the rapid development of distributed new energy, its penetration in the distribution network gradually increases, multiple microgrids in the same distribution network area need intergroup regulation and intergroup control, and the microgrid cluster technology that regulates and controls the microgrids in a grouping mode has begun to be explored in a large number of studies. This paper summarizes the research progress on the concepts of microgrids and microgrid clusters, organize network technology, topological structure, intergroup regulation and control, and operation modes, aiming to provide references for further research and practical applications of microgrid clusters.

articleTitle: Study on Key Factor Identification and Evaluation Methods of Quality Assurance Capabilities of Power Equipment Suppliers
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Building China into a strong nation in quality is an important measure to promote high-quality development and the transformation of China’s economy from large to strong. Strengthening the quality management of power equipment suppliers plays a crucial role in ensuring the safety and stability of the industrial and supply chains, and promoting high-quality economic development. This paper is based on the application of the quality assurance system of power equipment suppliers, and determines the measures and factor identification methods for building the assurance system. Based on the Analytic Hierarchy Process, an evaluation method of quality assurance capabilities of suppliers is established, and the weight index of the index at each level is given to quantify the quality assurance capabilities of suppliers, which helps to further improve the quality assurance level of suppliers.

articleTitle: Optimization Methodology for Electricity-Carbon Coupled Multilateral Trading Taking Into Account New Energy Consumption
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Electricity-carbon coupling is an emerging business field that can give full play to the advantages of electric power big data, take electric power as a link, and synergistically drive the whole society to realize green and low-carbon development. This paper analyzes the synergistic relationship between the power market and carbon market, and after clarifying the overall process of trading in the power and carbon market, establishes a joint trading model coupled with new energy and independent user direct trading model. The model guides the user-side resources to participate in new energy consumption. In the transaction process, the user obtains the revenue from new energy consumption, and the new energy power generation obtains the power generation quota by paying the user response cost, so as to improve the efficiency of power generation. Finally, the experiment proves the rationality of the joint dispatch mode of power generation right and carbon emission right, which realizes the efficient utilization of energy and cost reduction. At the same time, it provides a broader space for the large-scale consumption of wind power and promotes the development of the energy industry in the direction of green, low-carbon and sustainable.

articleTitle: Rural microgrid planning considering ice-plate sliding ice storage systems
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: The ice storage system utilizes ice as an energy storage medium, leveraging the significant latent heat during the phase transition of water. It produces and stores ice during off-peak electricity hours and melts the ice to release cooling during peak electricity hours to meet the cooling demand of rural cold storage facilities, thus achieving the effect of peak shaving and valley filling for the power grid. A linear model of the sliding ice-on-coil ice storage system considering the phase transition conditions, as well as a cold storage cooling load model, have been established. By coupling with the microgrid power system, the operational constraints and coordinated control of distributed power generation, power storage and ice storage are considered, and the superiority of the ice storage system is demonstrated by comparing with the conventional cooling system.

Author Keywords: Cooling and Electricity Coupled Microgrid Planning

articleTitle: Analysis of Seismic Resilience and Repair Economics of Complex Network Systems in Substations
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: The design of substation systems is characterized by its complexity and high level of integration, as it encompasses various types of electrical equipment housed within a confined building structure, interconnected through meticulously arranged wiring. This paper presents a methodology for evaluating the seismic resilience of substation systems, which integrates a directed graph model of power pathways with Simulink electrical simulations. The substation is conceptualized as a power transmission pathway formed by interconnected equipment and wiring, leading to the establishment of a directed graph model that represents the substation system network. An evaluation of seismic resilience is conducted from the perspective of a high-voltage multi-input to low-voltage multi-output system, yielding median values and logarithmic standard deviations of seismic capacity across different functional requirements. The failure probabilities associated with the ten outgoing lines of the substation are analyzed through nonlinear fitting, while Monte Carlo simulation is employed to assess the vulnerability of the substation system. By utilizing the actual electrical capacity of the substation system as a reference point, the overall functional state of the substation is characterized, and resilience indicators pertinent to seismic conditions in substations are proposed. Utilizing the strength-based assessment methodology outlined in FEMAP-58, a systematic evaluation of the maintenance costs for substations was conducted under three distinct seismic intensity conditions. This analysis delineated the probability distribution of maintenance costs across various numerical ranges and illustrated the probability distribution of the median maintenance cost (i.e., the P=50% quantile) within these ranges.

articleTitle: Framework analysis for smart grids in coping with new electricity system development dilemma
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Under the new situation of social development, the construction of a new electricity system is a key element for China to achieve the goal of “carbon peak & carbon neutral”, in which digital intelligence technology is a key component to support the development of power grids and to cope with the difficulties in the development of the new power system. In this study, the new dilemmas facing the development of the power generation, load and market sides are first studied from the perspective of deconstructing the new power system. Then, it analyses what benefits from and how digital intelligence technology upgrades the data flow ways to help power grid development and problem solving. Finally, the application of digital intelligence technology in power grids is collated and summarized, and a new type of framework depicting the characteristics and feathers of “digital intelligent power grids” is constructed, which provides a new idea and a general structure for the framework study of the development of smart grids.

articleTitle: Optimized Operation Model of Virtual Power Plant Considering Carbon Trading
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: In the face of global fossil energy shortages and environmental challenges, renewable energy generation, represented by wind and solar, is growing rapidly worldwide. However, these distributed energy sources are difficult to participate in the electricity market independently due to the volatility of their output. By integrating wind and solar power generation and energy storage systems and jointly participating in electricity market transactions, virtual power plants effectively solve the instability and randomness of distributed power generation in market operation. In addition, as an emerging participant in the power market, the virtual power plant’s participation in the carbon trading market not only helps to promote the utilization of new energy sources but also enhances its overall economic returns through environmental benefits. This study explores the optimization operation strategy of virtual power plants in the carbon trading and electricity market.

articleTitle: Research on the Two-Stage Optimization Method of Electric Thermal Storage Adjustable Load and Energy Storage Configuration for the Improvement of Renewable Energy Consumption Rate
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: With large-scale renewable energy connection of the power grid, the issue of renewable energy consumption is becoming increasingly prominent. This paper proposes a two-stage optimization method that utilizes electric thermal storage and energy storage to improve the local renewable energy consumption rate jointly. This paper first analyzes the working principle of electric thermal storage load and establishes an optimization model for electric thermal storage load operation with the objective function of maximizing local renewable energy consumption rate. Then, based on the optimization results of the previous stage, a bi-level optimization model for energy storage capacity configuration was established, with maximizing operational profits and minimizing energy storage investment as the inner and outer objective functions. This method can effectively improve the local renewable energy consumption rate and the economic efficiency of energy storage configuration. Finally, the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed method are verified through actual cases.

articleTitle: A Method for Extracting Risk Information of Scheduled Maintenance in Power Grids Based on Universal Information Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: To enhance fault prevention and handling guidance capabilities in the context of scheduled maintenance for power grids, this paper proposes a method for identifying entities in power dispatch texts based on a Universal Information Extraction (UIE) model. Focusing on risk forms for scheduled maintenance in power grids, this paper proposes an entity annotation method for extracting key information from these forms. By leveraging the general entity extraction capabilities of the Universal Information Extraction (UIE) model, we identify and output structured data from the unstructured text in the risk forms. This unified representation of textual entities enhances the representation capabilities of entity information. Utilizing the ERNIE 3.0 network to learn the contextual semantic features of sequences, we identify key information such as power grid equipment names, fault and anomaly types, and grid risk conditions. Experimental results indicate that the general information extraction model based on UIE achieves an F1 score of 95.78% on the scheduled maintenance risk form dataset. Validation with actual data from a specific power grid demonstrates that the proposed method has higher accuracy in power dispatch entity recognition compared to other algorithms, providing robust online support for power dispatch business scenarios.

articleTitle: Research on Internal Preheating Methods for Low-Temperature Lithium-Ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: To address the low-temperature deficiencies of batteries, this paper develops a temperature rise model for lithium-ion battery packs, integrating an equivalent circuit model with a thermal model based on the lithium plating criterion. Additionally, a multi-stage alternating current heating strategy is proposed to enhance the heating rate, taking into account the impact of temperature rise, and employing a variable amplitude heating method. Results indicate that this approach effectively prevents lithium plating, enabling the battery pack to be heated from -15° to above 0° within 435 seconds, significantly improving performance, lifespan, and reliability in low-temperature environments.

articleTitle: MLP-Transformers: Multi-Layer Perceptron coordinated Transformers for Time Series Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: This paper proposes MLP-Transformers, which combines multi-layer perceptron (MLP) and Transformer models to automatically divide time series data into batches and call the corresponding Transformer model for prediction. This method trains MLP and Transformer simultaneously during the training phase. First, a corresponding number of Transformer models and MLP models are created according to the number of categories of time series data, and then the training set is input into the MLP model for classification. Next, the most appropriate Transformer model is selected for training based on each batch of data to enhance the generalization ability of the model. During the prediction phase, the test set is fed into the trained MLP-Transformer model. After MLP classification, the corresponding Transformer model is used for prediction. Performances of MLP-Transformers are thoroughly evaluated using IEEE PHM 2012 dataset provided by FEMTO-ST Institute and jet engine lubrication oil dataset provided by airlines respectively. Experimental result shows that MLP-Transformers outperforms existing methods for dataset, demonstrating the effectiveness and the wide range applicability of the proposed method in solving time series problems.

Author Keywords: jet engine lubrication oil sensor data monitoring

articleTitle: Simulation and Optimal Design of Airflow Organization in Indoor Substation Based on Vortex Ventilation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: Under the condition of high temperature and high load, the ventilation and heat dissipation effect of indoor substations seriously affects the reliability and safety of substation operation. In this paper, vortex ventilation technology is introduced to take the main substation room of a 110 kV indoor substation in Beijing as the research object. Using Ansys Fluent numerical simulation, the indoor temperature field and velocity field characteristics of the main substation under the vortex ventilation form are explored. The results show that the vortex ventilation reduces the average temperature of the indoor personnel activity area by $11 \%$ compared with the original scheme. The maximum temperature at 0.3 m above the transformer was reduced by $22 \%$, and the heat accumulation between radiators and in the area above the transformer was improved. The effect of the location and size of the air supply outlet on heat dissipation by vortex ventilation was also studied in depth.

articleTitle: Digital Twin Early Warning of Operational Risks in Urban Underground Distribution Networks Considering Load Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: At present, the digital twin early warning node of urban underground distribution network operation risk generally adopts the range deployment form, and the coverage of early warning is small, which leads to the difficulty of the final unit early warning frequency reaching the expected standard. This paper proposes the design and practical analysis of the digital twin early warning method for urban underground distribution network operation risk considering the load characteristics.
