According to the current demand for early warning, data acquisition and load feature extraction shall be carried out first, the coverage of early warning shall be expanded by adopting adaptive method, and early warning adaptive monitoring nodes shall be deployed to build a digital twin early warning model of load characteristics distribution network operation risk, and the digital twin early warning of risk shall be realized by tracking identification and correction processing. The test results show that: in the selected three test areas, under the selected operating environment of light rain, moderate rain, heavy rain and rainstorm, the unit early warning frequency calculated this time can reach more than 155 Hz, which indicates that with the help of load characteristics, the designed digital twin early warning of urban underground distribution network operation risk is more effective and targeted, The efficiency of early warning has also been significantly improved.

articleTitle: Research on Inertia Evaluation Method for Large Receiving-End Power Systems under the Background of New Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: With the acceleration of global energy transition, the new-type power system, characterized by its cleanliness, low carbon emissions, and high efficiency, has emerged as a crucial development direction for future energy systems. However, the large-scale integration of renewable energy generation units has significantly altered the system inertia characteristics, posing challenges to the stable operation of power systems. This paper reviews the research progress in inertia assessment methods for large-scale receiving-end power systems under the background of new-type power systems, focusing on model-based, data-driven, and hybrid inertia assessment techniques. Furthermore, it discusses the challenges faced and future development directions. By providing this comprehensive overview, the paper aims to offer reference and inspiration for researchers and practitioners in the field of power system inertia assessment.

articleTitle: Exploration and application of new energy system construction path for ultra-large urban central business district
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: With the increasingly prominent peak load in the urban core area of high-temperature and high-humidity regions and the growing impact of electric vehicle charging load, the region faces significant pressure on power supply guarantee, weak flexibility in adjustment, and low level of intelligence. The proposal of a new energy system effectively alleviates the problems of energy network development and supply and demand matching. The project aims to build China’s first large-scale interconnected, flexible and intelligent, safe and reliable “world-class exemplary scene of a new energy system in the urban core area of a super-large city,” focusing on the “energy-electricity-cooling” three energy networks, and innovatively integrating the “car-station-building-network-city” green energy technology path. It will focus on building a number of photovoltaic and energy storage super-charging stations, low-carbon flexible buildings, group-style high-efficiency cooling and green hub projects, integrating car-grid interaction, virtual power plants, and intelligent gas pipeline technologies, to achieve the friendly integration and management of the energy system. It will realize the leading innovative functions of city-level and regional-level energy system flexibility and support, create an international leading smart new power system with the characteristics of “green and efficient, flexible and open, and digitally enabled,” explore replicable and scalable exemplary pathways of a new energy system, and create an international benchmark project to achieve advanced urban district demonstration.

articleTitle: Influence of Inrush Current of Converter Transformer on High-voltage DC System Based on Unbalanced Residual Magnetism
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: In high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission systems, the inrush current of the converter transformer can have severe impacts on the system. This paper establishes a model of an ±800kV DC transmission system based on the imbalanced remanence characteristics of the converter transformer. It calculates and analyzes the effects of inrush current on the primary side of the converter transformer and the AC bus. A comparative analysis is conducted between the inrush current under imbalanced and balanced residual magnetism, examining the inrush current characteristics through the content of the inrush current and the proportion of total harmonics under different types and levels of remanence. Finally, the paper compares and analyzes the suppression effects of two closing strategies on the inrush current caused by remanence. The research presented in this paper provides certain guiding significance for comprehensively understanding the impact of residual magnetism in the converter transformer core on inrush current, as well as the impact of inrush current on AC systems.

articleTitle: Green Procurement Evaluation of Digitalized Smart Grid Based on Shapley-RM Method
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Smart Grids and Energy Systems (SGES)
abstract: In the context of smart energy and digitalization, the problem of difficult coupling between the traditional supply chain cost evaluation and the green evaluation has become more prominent, facing many challenges in practice. To this end, a comprehensive and practical green procurement cost evaluation frame is constructed, where the nonlinear relationship between indicators and the time span of cost evaluation are comprehensively considered, and the Shapley-RM method, a cost evaluation model that combines the Shapley value and the digital reputation mechanism, is proposed. In the field of smart energy, the model is able to effectively integrate real-time energy procurement and green goals by dynamically coupling evaluation dimensions and evaluation cycles. In a data-driven digital environment, the Shapley-RM methodology leverages cross-timescale full-life-cycle procurement big data in the energy supply chain to help companies optimize their procurement decisions and balance cost and environmental benefits. Application analysis of the model shows that the Shapley-RM approach can effectively support green procurement decisions in smart energy, provide precise and intelligent support for enterprises in the dynamic and complex energy market, and promote the deep integration of green and digital transformation.
